newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act's Prebble calls for mending of U.S. ties.
newsitem.headline: Act's Prebble calls for mending of U.S. ties.

text.p: Act New Zealand leader Richard Prebble called on Tuesday for a mending of defence relations with the United States, saying this could lead in turn to better trade ties.
"I believe we can be nuclear free and have a sensible relationship with the leader of the free world," Prebble said in a speech in Wellington.
"After the U.S. presidential elections we have a window of opportunity to make a determined effort to resolve our differences with the United States.

"Putting our relationship back on a normal basis will not only enable us to have a credible foreign and defence policy, it will also enable us to resolve some important trade issues. The present government feels unable to raise legitimate problems that we have with the USA."
Washington froze defence ties and intelligence cooperation in the mid-1980s after New Zealand banned visits by nuclear-armed and nuclear-powered ships.

In a normal relationship, Prebble said, the two sides could talk constructively on how to address New Zealand's trade deficit with the United States, which was proportionately greater than the U.S. deficits with China and Japan combined.
Prebble said New Zealand must decide if it needed defence forces or not.
If not, it was wasting NZ$1 billion a year. If it did, then the defence forces needed strengthening.

"Our armed forces should be like the America's Cup squad -- small, elite, professional, and equal to the best in the world. The cheapest and quickest way to do that is to resolve our dispute with the USA," Prebble said.
